title: Augmentations and canonicity of an abelian Čech comparison
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $U_i$ any family of opens, $F$ an abelian sheaf [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology], and $F\to I^\bullet$ an injective resolution [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Write $A=\Gamma(X,I^\bullet)$ and $D^{p,q}=\check C^p(U,I^q)$, with Čech degree first and total differential $d_C+(-1)^p d_I$ [def-sp-double-complex-total]. Define $\alpha:A\to\mathrm{Tot}(D)$ by restriction into the $(0,q)$ summand and $\beta:\check C(U,F)\to\mathrm{Tot}(D)$ by the coefficient augmentation into the $(p,0)$ summand. Both are genuine chain maps. A map $c:\check H^q(U,F)\to H^q(X,F)$ is canonical if the following holds on every injective resolution: for every Čech class $x$, every cocycle $a:\mathbf Z_X\to I^q$, and every section cycle $z$ whose underlying section is the value at $1$ of $a$ under the constant-sheaf adjunction, $c(x)=\operatorname{extMk}_I(a)$ implies $H^q(\beta)(x)=H^q(\alpha)([z])$. Every Ext class has a representing cocycle and every such cocycle gives a section cycle; thus this is the usual augmentation quotient equation without any arbitrary choice of cohomology isomorphism. Neither degree-zero normalization nor a boundary law is part of this predicate.
